\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Privacy (RQ3). Percentage of the split seeds where the modification does not do worse than vanilla on the same split, with the mean and standard deviation of the paired differences in parentheses, in the units of the metric. A configuration with no systematic effect splits the seeds evenly, so 50\% means no difference. The reference row is the unmodified baseline, $w$ is the reweighted reconstruction loss, $t$ is the added balance term, and the subscript is the magnitude. The mean and standard deviation are the paired difference of the excess over 50, which is the same quantity the percentage counts, so a negative mean means the modification carries less leakage than vanilla. A seed where neither the modification nor vanilla goes above 50 contributes exactly zero, so a dataset that never leaks shows a column of zeros: that is the metric saying there was nothing to leak, not a missing value.}
\label{tab:stats-privacy}
